owned-dotnet-callback-results:
    name: Callback-result lifetimes in installed NuGet packages
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 240
    env:
      EMCC_CORES: "2"
    steps:
      - name: Check out the exact revision
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
      - name: Select Python 3.11 for backported type aliases
        id: callback_python311
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Select Python 3.12 for standard-library type aliases
        id: callback_python312
        uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Select Ruby 3.3
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          ruby-version: '3.3.12'
      - name: Select .NET 8 SDK
        uses: actions/setup-dotnet@v6
        with:
          dotnet-version: '8.0.424'
      - name: Install callback acceptance tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y build-essential cmake git jq libgmp-dev libuv1-dev m4 pkg-config python3-venv ripgrep zstd
          npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
          bash scripts/bootstrap-toolchains.sh
          bash scripts/bootstrap-rust-ci.sh
          python3 -m pip download --no-cache-dir --only-binary=:all: --no-deps --dest build/python-typing-wheels/4.6.0 typing_extensions==4.6.0
          python3 -m pip download --no-cache-dir --only-binary=:all: --no-deps --dest build/python-typing-wheels/4.16.0 typing_extensions==4.16.0
          python3 -m venv build/python-collection-typecheck
          build/python-collection-typecheck/bin/python -m pip install --no-cache-dir mypy==2.3.1 typing_extensions==4.16.0 mypy_extensions==1.1.0 pathspec==1.1.1 librt==0.15.0 ast-serialize==0.11.2
      - name: Install all callback browser engines
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium firefox webkit
      - name: Build the callback shared runtime
        shell: bash

          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p build
          bash scripts/build-lean-link-spike.sh 2>&1 | tee build/owned-dotnet-callback-result-runtime.log
          test -s build/lean-link-spike/lazy/main.wasm

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          source scripts/env.sh
          export LEAN_BRIDGE_DOTNET="$(command -v dotnet)"
          export LEAN_BRIDGE_RUBY="$(command -v ruby)"
          export LEAN_BRIDGE_GEM="$(command -v gem)"

          rg '^# pass 26$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-results.log
          rg '^# fail 0$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-results.log
          rg '^# cancelled 0$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-results.log
          rg '^# skipped 0$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-results.log
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-no-host.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-no-host-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-host.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-host-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-no-host-process.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-no-host-sanitizers.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-no-host-package.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined-process.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined-sanitizers.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined-package.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/ordinary-combined-release.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-no-host.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-no-host-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-host.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-host-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-combined.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-combined-lifetime.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-no-host-process.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-no-host-sanitizers.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-no-host-package.json
          test -s build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/reviewed-combined-process.json

        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          npm run test:owned-dotnet-callback-evidence 2>&1 | tee build/owned-dotnet-callback-evidence.log
          rg '^# tests 8$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-evidence.log
          rg '^# pass 8$' build/owned-dotnet-callback-evidence.log

## .NET callback-result lifetimes

Run these gates in order with .NET SDK 8.0.424, the pinned Lean, Rust and
Emscripten tools, Ruby 3.3, the Python setup below and all three Playwright
browsers:

```sh
npm run test:owned-dotnet-callback-results
npm run test:owned-dotnet-callback-evidence
```

Set `LEAN_BRIDGE_DOTNET` to the `dotnet` executable. On glibc 2.36, set
`LEAN_BRIDGE_NATIVE_TEST_GLIBC_FLOOR=2.36`. The first gate requires 26 tests
without skips and retains 26 reports under `build/owned-dotnet-callback-results/`.
The second gate runs eight tests that reconstruct those reports' runtime and
package inputs, generated bindings and public consumer probes across all seven
ecosystems, and rejects altered claims.
It runs after execution because it reads the newly produced reports.

Both ordinary Lean source and reviewed IR exercise native closure results
anchored to their original argument owner, raw and whole-value host replies,
higher-order callbacks, multiple callback arguments, receiver methods and
consuming calls. Optimized managed probes force collections during reads and
callback replies, exercise concurrent close and creator-thread exit, and check
allocation failures before and after ownership transfer. Compiled mutations
must fail before the restored bindings pass again.

NuGet tests compare independently built archives, reject modified contracts
and generated sources, and compile valid and invalid consumers against the
installed assembly. They delete producer sources and the CLI before consumer
installation, then remove consumer sources, package caches and handoff archives
before SDK-free relocated execution. The installed consumers also check fork
rejection and runtime retirement, including host replies and consuming calls.
The combined release installs C, C++, Rust, Python, Ruby, NuGet and npm packages
from one build and exercises npm in browser pages, React and workers.

AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer instrument the native adapter
called by the C# probe. Positive fault controls must trigger both detectors.
The Lean runtime and CLR are not instrumented; native allocation and identity
ledgers check cleanup. LeakSanitizer is disabled for these managed runs.
CI requires both gates, rejects skipped cases and retains their logs and
reports as `dotnet-callback-results` artifacts.
C, C++, Rust, Python, Ruby, C# and npm also accept [callback-result anchors](../publish/c.md#anchor-a-callback-result-to-its-argument).

### Anchor a callback result to its argument

Keep `resources` and `ownedAggregates`, and place the lifetime inside the
export's `callable.result` contract. For `Owned.makeRecord` with type
`Bundle → Bool → Bundle → Bundle`, select one outer argument with
`"arities": { "Owned.makeRecord": 1 }`. The returned function takes two
arguments. Place this object under `contracts["Owned.makeRecord"]` to anchor
its result to its second argument:

```json
{
  "result": {
    "ownership": "lease",
    "lifetime": { "scope": "explicit", "anchor": null },
    "callable": {
      "result": {
        "ownership": "borrow",
        "lifetime": { "scope": "parameter", "anchor": "arg1" }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Argument names belong to the returned function, not the outer export or its
private closure handle. Reviewed Binding IR records the same decision on the
callable result; both authoring paths pass through the Lean compiler.

C# callers pass `Value<Bundle>` for the selected argument. Its original owner
controls the result's lifetime even when the function returns captured data.
The result and borrowed descendants expire together, including empty values.
`Retain()` and `Api.CopyValue` create independent owners. See the
[consumer examples](../consume/dotnet.md#callback-results-borrowed-from-an-argument).

Host delegates receive raw borrowed arguments and return `CallbackResult<T>`.
An implicit conversion accepts a raw reply or a whole `Value<T>`, including a
recovery reply. The bridge checks and converts the reply before the borrowed
frame expires. Native closures use typed overloads that preserve their original
identity; their anchored `Invoke` still requires the selected whole owner.
Callback storage remains call-scoped. This contract does not enable asynchronous
delivery or transfer callback inputs.

Build with `--target nuget`. These packages use `owned-dotnet-v5`, managed
ownership contract and NuGet receipt version 5, and native ownership model
version 6. Packaging reconstructs the callback contracts and generated C# from
compiler-authenticated metadata. Callback-result anchors do not require
export-result anchors, receiver members, consuming inputs or host callbacks.
Packages without callback-result anchors retain their existing receipt versions.
